name: t3code
description: The best way to control Claude Code, Codex and more from any computer or phone
readmeExcerpt:
T3 Code

The open-source control plane for coding agents.

Download · iOS · Android · Web · Docs · Discord

T3 Code runs the coding agents on your machine and gives them one fast interface. Start a thread at your desk, then approve the next step from your phone. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any [ACP](./docs/user/providers-acp.md) agent. If an agent is set up on your computer, T3 Code can control it. ## What you get - **Your subscriptions.** T3 Code does not resell tokens. It drives the agents you are already signed in to. - **Every agent in one place.** Change models in the middle of a thread. Let Claude hand a task to Codex. - **Desktop, web, and phone.** One server, and every client shows the same threads. There are apps for iOS and Android. - **Remote ready.** Run agents on any machine. Connect over your local network, Tailscale, or [T3 Connect](./docs/user/remote-access.md). - **Git built in.** Each thread can work in its own worktree. Review the diff, then commit, push, and open a pull request with one button. - **Fast.** Performance is a feature here. We measure it, and we treat a dropped frame as a bug. - **Open.** MIT licensed. If you don't like something, fork it. ## Install ### Desktop app [Download T3 Code](https://t3.codes/download) for macOS, Windows, or Linux. You can also use a package manager: | Platform | Command | | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | | macOS | `brew install --cask t3-code` | | Windows | `winget install T3Tools.T3Code` or `scoop install extras/t3code` | | Arch Linux | `yay -S t3code-bin` | | Nix | `nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code` | | Debian, Ubuntu | `.deb` from [Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases) | ### Command line This installs the `t3` command. Run `t3` to start the server and open the web app. ```bash curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh ``` On Windows, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex ``` To try it once without an install, run `npx t3@latest`. ### Phone Get the app from the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/t3-code-remote-claude-more/id6787819824) or [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.t3tools.t3code). Then follow [remote access](./docs/user/remote-access.md) to connect it to your computer. ### Sign in to an agent T3 Code needs one agent that is installed and signed in. For example, install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and run `claude auth login`, or install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`. [Provider setup](./docs/user/install.md#providers) has the steps for each agent. [Install T3 Code](./docs/user/install.md) covers nightly builds, AppImage, WSL, and NixOS. ## "Wait, what are you selling me?" Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar. We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the tool that you want. ## Documentation - [Install and first run](./docs/user/install.md) - [Remote access from a phone or another machine](./docs/user/remote-access.md) - [Permission modes](./docs/user/permission-modes.md) - [Source control](./docs/user/source-control.md) - [Connect outside agents over MCP](./docs/user/outside-agents.md) - [FAQ](./docs/user/faq.md) [All docs](./docs/README.md) has the full list. ## Contributing We have limited review capacity. Small, focused fixes are the most likely to be merged. Features need an approved discussion first. - Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before you report a bug or open a pull request. - Put feature requests in [Ideas](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/categories/ideas). - Build from source with the [development runbook](./docs/operations/development.md#first-checkout). The [architecture overview](./docs/internals/overview.md) explains how it works. - Get help in [Discord](https://discord.gg/jn4EGJjrvv). ## License [MIT](./LICENSE)

aiSummary.oneLiner: An intuitive management GUI and agent harness control surface for interacting with AI coding assistants.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: T3Code provides a unified, web-based graphical interface designed to orchestrate and manage autonomous AI coding agents like Claude Code and OpenCode. It replaces the traditional command-line experience with a visual dashboard, making it easier for developers to manage complex AI workflows. The harness allows users to monitor agent progress in real-time, review proposed code diffs visually, and manage intricate prompt engineering tasks. By abstracting the terminal interactions, it lowers the barrier to entry for managing multi-agent systems. It is built to seamlessly interface with existing agent CLI tools in the background.
keyFeatures: Unified Dashboard: Provides a single web interface to oversee and orchestrate multiple different coding agents simultaneously.
Visual Code Review: Renders AI-generated code diffs in a clear, browser-based view rather than forcing users to read terminal output.
Prompt Management: Includes tools for inputting, saving, and visually tweaking complex prompts before sending them to an agent.
Real-Time Monitoring: Streams agent logs and execution steps directly to the GUI for continuous oversight of the AI's progress.
Broad Agent Compatibility: Designed with an extensible architecture to support various agents including Codex, Claude, and Cursor.

**v0.1.11-nightly.20261117.4825** · 62 changes from 18 contributors

- **Issue tracking.** Browse, filter, update, and link issues to threads across GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Forgejo, and Linear.
- **Saved filter views.** Save named filter views for pull requests and issues instead of rebuilding filters each time.
- **Sparse worktrees.** Configure sparse checkout patterns for new worktrees to avoid checking out entire large repositories.
- **Thread model options.** Choose model options when starting a thread with the CLI.
- **Usage history retention.** Keep usage history longer by configuring retention for each environment.
- **Edit from here.** Grok, Kiro, Antigravity, and other supported agents retain the conversation when you edit from an earlier message.
- **Shared SSH hosts.** Older desktop clients no longer interrupt running agent work by replacing a newer server on a shared SSH host.

releases.name: T3 Code v0.1.10
releases.body:
**v0.1.10** · 1924 changes from 360 contributors

- **Reply to responses.** Reply directly to an assistant response so your message identifies the response it refers to.
- **Theme customization.** Use custom theme colors, CSS, and full-size background images to change the app’s appearance.
- **Windows server updates.** Run T3 Code as a Windows service and update it remotely instead of restarting it by hand.
- **Keep agents working.** T3 Code keeps your computer awake while agents are working, then releases it afterward.
- **T3 Connect device approval.** Require approval on a host before new T3 Connect devices can access it.
- **Native resume.** Resume stopped Claude, Codex, OpenCode, and Cursor threads without adding a new user message.
- **Settings languages.** Choose from nine languages for supported Settings text without reloading the app.

### Plus 1811 more bug fixes and performance improvements.

readmeHtml:
T3 Code

The open-source control plane for coding agents.

Download · iOS · Android · Web · Docs · Discord

T3 Code runs the coding agents on your machine and gives them one fast interface. Start a thread at your desk, then approve the next step from your phone.

It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any ACP agent. If an agent is set up on your computer, T3 Code can control it.

What you get

  • Your subscriptions. T3 Code does not resell tokens. It drives the agents you are already signed in to.
  • Every agent in one place. Change models in the middle of a thread. Let Claude hand a task to Codex.
  • Desktop, web, and phone. One server, and every client shows the same threads. There are apps for iOS and Android.
  • Remote ready. Run agents on any machine. Connect over your local network, Tailscale, or T3 Connect.
  • Git built in. Each thread can work in its own worktree. Review the diff, then commit, push, and open a pull request with one button.
  • Fast. Performance is a feature here. We measure it, and we treat a dropped frame as a bug.
  • Open. MIT licensed. If you don't like something, fork it.

Install

Desktop app

Download T3 Code for macOS, Windows, or Linux. You can also use a package manager:

Platform Command
macOS brew install --cask t3-code
Windows winget install T3Tools.T3Code or scoop install extras/t3code
Arch Linux yay -S t3code-bin
Nix nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code
Debian, Ubuntu .deb from Releases

Command line

This installs the t3 command. Run t3 to start the server and open the web app.

curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh

On Windows, in PowerShell:

irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex

To try it once without an install, run npx t3@latest.

Phone

Get the app from the App Store or Google Play. Then follow remote access to connect it to your computer.

Sign in to an agent

T3 Code needs one agent that is installed and signed in. For example, install Claude Code and run claude auth login, or install Codex CLI and run codex login.

Provider setup has the steps for each agent. Install T3 Code covers nightly builds, AppImage, WSL, and NixOS.

"Wait, what are you selling me?"

Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar.

We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the tool that you want.

Documentation

  • Install and first run
  • Remote access from a phone or another machine
  • Permission modes
  • Source control
  • Connect outside agents over MCP
  • FAQ

All docs has the full list.

Contributing

We have limited review capacity. Small, focused fixes are the most likely to be merged. Features need an approved discussion first.

  • Read CONTRIBUTING.md before you report a bug or open a pull request.
  • Put feature requests in Ideas.
  • Build from source with the development runbook. The architecture overview explains how it works.
  • Get help in Discord.

License

MIT
